{{< include /knowledge/includes/setup-parameters.qmd >}}

**STATUS: DRAFT.** Requires securities, derivative-litigation, Rule 14a-8, and damages counsel review before sending or filing.

**COST TO FILE:** $200 to $600 for one share of stock (pro bono lawyer).

**PROBABILITY THE MATH REACHES THE BOARD:** approximately 100%. The Board is legally required to read what the corporate secretary receives by certified mail.

**WHAT IT BUYS:** approximately {{< var dfda_trial_capacity_plus_efficacy_lag_lives_saved_nounit >}} fewer humans dying of cancer, Alzheimer's, ALS, and cardiovascular disease, by compressing the untreated-disease queue from {{< var status_quo_queue_clearance_years >}} to {{< var dfda_queue_clearance_years >}} [@1-percent-treaty-paper-2025] [@1-pct-treaty-impact-paper-2025]. The dead include, in expectation, members of your family, members of the defendants' families, and members of the judge's family. The price of the share buys one named human a legally enforceable obligation to read why.

::: {.callout-warning}
**Legal posture for reviewing counsel.** The public wrapper is morally aggressive. The board-facing demand is narrower. In *McRitchie v. Zuckerberg*, C.A. No. 2022-0890-JTL (Del. Ch. Apr. 30, 2024), Vice Chancellor Laster rejected a fiduciary-duty theory based on directors' obligation to consider society-wide or macroeconomic interests. Delaware law applies the single-firm, shareholder-primacy model.

The love letter therefore does not ask directors to save the world as a charitable act. It asks whether a recurring corporate expenditure benefits this company's shareholders after accounting for the effect of military-budget-ratchet lobbying on the economy that funds future contracts, shareholder income, shareholder survival, and long-term market value.

Target doctrine: *Caremark* 2.0 duty of oversight, as expanded in *Marchand v. Barnhill* (2019) and *Garfield v. Allen* (2024, V.C. Laster). The love letter itself creates the "red flag" that triggers oversight obligations.

Derivative recovery usually belongs to the corporation, not the filing shareholder. Direct personal damages are an aggressive and unlikely theory. Rule 14a-8 is a separate eligible-shareholder path with ownership and holding requirements. Do not promise plaintiffs a direct payout from derivative recovery.
:::

## What This Document Is (Read This Part If You Just Got Forwarded This Link)

This is the funniest lawsuit in the universe and this page is everything you need to file it.

It is the first lawsuit in legal history where the defendants are radically better off losing than winning. Settling adds approximately {{< var avg_life_extension_per_beneficiary >}} to each defendant's healthy life and approximately {{< var treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} to the average shareholder's lifetime income. Winning leaves the defendant where they started: facing the same diseases on the same timeline, while their lobbying continues to keep the cure trials underfunded.


### What You Personally Get From Filing

| Benefit | Approximate value |
|---|---:|
| Additional healthy life expectancy if treaty passes | ~{{< var avg_life_extension_per_beneficiary >}} |
| Additional lifetime income if treaty passes | ~{{< var treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} |
| Ordinary shareholder exposure to the company you file against | Uncertain; the stock can rise or fall while the campaign is pending |
| Personal share of the recovered lifespan of the {{< var dfda_trial_capacity_plus_efficacy_lag_lives_saved_nounit >}} humans the campaign prevents from dying | Not pricable; this is the part the love letter is about |
| Standing to tell the people you love that you tried | This one is free; you just have to file |

The cost is one share (~$200) plus 43 hours of work. Under the [Part 3](#part-3-expected-value-for-plaintiffs) assumptions (ten defendants sued, 5% per-defendant probability of a redirection), the modeled upside is mostly treaty value, life expectancy, and the value of a larger economy, not a direct litigation payout.

### How To File (60-Second Version)

1. Buy 1 share of any major military contractor. The eight with [pre-filled fact sheets](pre-filled-demand-letters.qmd) are RTX, LMT, BA, GD, NOC, LHX, HII, and LDOS. Others (BAH, CACI, SAIC, BAE, Thales) work too; you just look up the corporate-secretary address yourself.
2. Copy the love letter below, fill in the bracketed fields, sign it.
3. Send it certified mail to the corporate secretary of the defendant.
4. Wait 60 days. Use the [post-response decision tree](#board-response-three-outcomes) when the board responds.

If you want company on the way: [how to find a lawyer](#the-counsel-pitch), [filing-day checklist](filing-day-checklist.qmd), [pre-filled defendant fact sheets](pre-filled-demand-letters.qmd), and [the media kit](plaintiff-media-kit.qmd) are all linked.

If you want to read the full argument before deciding: [Where Am I Wrong?](where-am-i-wrong.qmd) is the most rigorous version of the math, and [The Eisenhower Curve](../economics/eisenhower-curve.qmd) is the strategic-competition version of why the current allocation makes the country weaker, not stronger.

The rest of this document is the love letter itself, the legal theory, the outcome matrix, and the operational templates. The Open Letter to the Boards (below) is the version of the love letter you can post on social media unchanged. The numbered love letter in Part 1 is the version you send by certified mail.

## An Open Letter to the Boards

To the board members and CEOs of every military contractor named in this campaign:

We love you and we do not want you and everyone you have ever loved to die of pancreatic cancer, ovarian cancer, brain cancer, Alzheimer's, ALS, Parkinson's, or heart disease. We do not want your husband or wife, your kids, or your parents to die of those things. We do not want our own families to die of them either. We are in the same boat. I am going to suffer and die. So is my mom. So is everyone I have ever loved. So are you.

Sometime in the next ten years, someone you love is going to get a diagnosis. It will most likely be one of the four diseases above. The treatment that could have cured it will not exist, because the trial that would have produced it was not funded, because the Company's lobbying budget you signed off on this year was pointed at the wrong thing. You will spend weeks visiting them in the hospital. You will rearrange your schedule around their chemotherapy. You will sit in a waiting room while a doctor explains what "palliative" means. You will go to their funeral. You will go to the wake. You will drive home and sit in your car in the driveway for a while.

We do not want that for you. Your Company's lobbying is making it more likely. Every human reading this is going to die of some disease, and the disease will almost certainly be one that could have been cured if someone had funded the trial. Right now the lobbying you authorize maintains a world that spends {{< var military_to_government_clinical_trials_spending_ratio >}} times more on the military than on testing which medicines cure those diseases. That ratio is killing you. It is also making your family poorer than they would otherwise be. And your net worth is going to be zero if you are dead, unless you are buried with your money, which your kids are unlikely to do.

The Company's lobbying budget for {{< var nuclear_winter_overkill_factor_nounit >}} apocalypses worth of mass-murder capacity, at the expense of the clinical trials that would cure the diseases that will kill you and everyone you love, is the specific corporate decision we are asking you to revisit.

We are not asking you to do something. We are asking you to *stop* doing something. Specifically, stop signing the lobbying line item that is shortening your own life. The same budget that currently funds the most effective political-influence operation on Earth, pointed at maintaining the {{< var military_to_government_clinical_trials_spending_ratio >}}-to-1 ratio that is killing all of us, just needs to be pointed at the [1% treaty](../solution/1-percent-treaty.qmd) [@1-percent-treaty-paper-2025] [@1-pct-treaty-impact-paper-2025] instead. Same lobbyists. Same congressional relationships. Same dinners with senators. Different ask.

What that looks like concretely: on the Monday morning after you sign the settlement, the same military-industry lobbyists who currently spend their days arguing against any redirection of military spending will, in the same offices, with the same access, start arguing for the 1% treaty. Nothing in your operations changes. Nothing in your supply chain changes. Nothing in your customer relationships changes. The only thing that changes is what your lobbyists are saying on Capitol Hill. That is the entire change. That is what saves you, your family, your shareholders, and us.

The known-safe pharmaceutical compounds that would cure the diseases that will kill you are sitting in the trial queue right now, waiting for funding. **Metformin** for Alzheimer's. **Rapamycin** for biological aging. **Low-dose naltrexone** for autoimmune conditions and certain cancers. These three molecules alone have public research support; {{< var safe_compounds_count_nounit >}} known-safe compounds total are in the same queue, with {{< var unexplored_ratio >}} of their potential disease indications never tested. The 1% redirection funds those trials. The current lobbying keeps the money pointed somewhere else.

The lawsuit is the only mechanism we have to put the math in front of you in a form you are legally required to read. If you read it and we are wrong, please tell us how. If you read it and we are right, please act on it. Either way, we love you.

If you are inclined to defend the current allocation on national-security grounds, please read [The Eisenhower Curve](../economics/eisenhower-curve.qmd) before responding. The short version: the current allocation is the mechanism by which the United States is losing strategic competition to China. The treaty is the most pro-military action available. The country that won World War II had {{< var us_1939_military_spending_pct_lower_than_current >}} less military spending than the United States has today, and the reason it won is that its productive economy had not been cannibalized to fund a peacetime military.

One more thing. As far as we can tell, this is the first lawsuit ever where the defendants are way better off losing than winning. Settling costs your Company nothing. It adds approximately {{< var treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} to the average shareholder's lifetime income, because the economy grows about {{< var treaty_trajectory_gdp_vs_current_trajectory_multiplier_year_15 >}} bigger at year 15 when disease stops eating it. (You are well above the average and would gain more.) It adds approximately {{< var avg_life_extension_per_beneficiary >}} of healthy life to the average beneficiary, including you, your spouse, your kids, your parents, and every shareholder you serve. We looked for any version where fighting helps you. There isn't one.

To say it plainly: winning this case kills you. If you beat us in court, the lobbying keeps going. If the lobbying keeps going, the line of untested cures stays {{< var status_quo_queue_clearance_years_nounit >}} years long. The diseases that will kill you, your wife or husband, your kids, your shareholders, and us stay in that line. Winning this case in court is the same as signing your own death warrant on behalf of everyone you love. We are filing the lawsuit because we do not want you to sign it. We do not want to die either.

The same math applies to every human in the case: the judge, the jury, the defense lawyer, and all of their families. The judge who throws this case out is throwing out the case that would have helped the judge live longer, helped the judge's wife or husband live longer, and helped the judge's kids and grandkids live longer. The defense lawyer who wins a motion to dismiss is winning a motion that, on average, kills them, their spouse, and their kids a decade or two early. Same for every juror. Same for every juror's family.

Add it up. Every person named in the case has about 10 to 20 people they love. Across the plaintiff, the defendants, the judge, the jury, and the lawyers on both sides, that is roughly 100 to 300 humans whose lives get shorter or longer based on what this court decides. We love all of them and we do not want any of them to die of horrible diseases the math says we could cure. This case is a letter asking every human reading it to choose to live longer and let everyone they have ever loved live longer.

Military contractors exist for one reason. They exist to preserve the lives of the citizens whose government funds them. Their charter, their privileges, their contracts, and their lobbying access all flow from that purpose and from no other. The lobbying your Board currently authorizes maintains {{< var nuclear_winter_overkill_factor_nounit >}} apocalypses worth of mass-murder capacity while withholding the funding that would produce the treatments your shareholders, your families, and your fellow citizens require to survive pancreatic cancer, ovarian cancer, glioblastoma, Alzheimer's, ALS, Parkinson's, and cardiovascular disease. The Company is a military contractor producing, in the aggregate, an unprotected population. We ask you to redirect the lobbying so the Company performs the function for which it exists.

Defense counsel exist to represent the client. The client is the Company. The Company has no interests except those of the humans who compose it. Under Delaware law, those interests are the interests of the shareholders, who are humans who must be alive to receive financial returns and whose families must be alive for those returns to mean anything. Under ABA Model Rule 2.1, counsel must render candid advice on the economic and moral considerations relevant to those humans' situation. The math in this filing shows that settling adds approximately {{< var treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} to the average shareholder's lifetime income and approximately {{< var avg_life_extension_per_beneficiary >}} to the average shareholder's healthy life, in an economy roughly {{< var treaty_trajectory_gdp_vs_current_trajectory_multiplier_year_15 >}} larger than the current trajectory at year 15. Whether the Company itself grows, shrinks, or pivots into medical and biotech work in that larger economy is a question for the Board to answer; the shareholders' interests are served by settling either way. Counsel rendering candid advice on those humans' interests reaches one conclusion. Counsel advising "fight" is advising every human the corporation comprises to act against their own interest. We ask counsel to advise the Board accurately.

Courts exist to promote the general welfare. The general welfare is not an abstraction. It is the median health and the median wealth of the citizens the law was written to protect. The math in this filing shows that a procedural dismissal of this case shortens the median citizen's healthy life expectancy and reduces the median citizen's lifetime income by approximately {{< var treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}}. A court that dismisses this case on procedural grounds is exercising the power the Constitution granted it to do the opposite of what the Constitution granted that power for. We ask the court to permit the case to proceed so the institution performs the function for which it exists.

To the judge: if you are still leaning toward throwing this case out on a technicality, we are asking you to do one thing before signing the order. Take a piece of paper. Write down, in your own handwriting, the name of the person you love most in the world. Look at that name. Under the math in this filing, that is the person whose life your order makes shorter. We are not asking you to rule against the law. We are asking you to read the math, write the name, and then decide. The law belongs to you and to the bar. The name belongs to you alone. We are asking you not to write it.

## Why This Works

The military lobby is the most effective political-influence operation on Earth. It spends approximately {{< var defense_lobbying_annual >}} per year buying politicians and receives hundreds of billions of dollars in military contracts in return. Outbidding it is impossible. The lawsuit redirects it instead.

The military industry's lobbying machine produces negative ROI for its own shareholders. Military contractors are humans who die of the same diseases as everyone else. They live in the same economy that their lobbying is keeping small. They are not a sophisticated adversary defending a rational interest. They are an unsupervised line item on a corporate budget that nobody has ever ROI-analyzed because nobody had to.

There is precedent for a board lobbying itself into the ground. The Ethyl Gasoline Corporation, a joint venture of General Motors and Standard Oil, lobbied for decades to keep tetraethyl lead in gasoline, because it held the patents and you cannot patent ethanol [@kovarik-leaded-gasoline-history-2005] [@kitman-secret-history-lead-2000]. The lead cost Americans 824 million IQ points, including the directors' own children's [@mcfarland-lead-iq-2022]. Run the numbers and even Ethyl's shareholders would have ended up roughly {{< var ethyl_shareholder_counterfactual_wealth_gain >}} richer had the board switched to ethanol in 1923, because a diversified portfolio lives in the economy the brain damage shrank [@jones-schneider-iq-growth-2006]. Nobody on that board ever saw an ROI analysis of the lobbying either. The product changed. The unsupervised line item did not.

Once a single board receives a sourced, quantitative analysis showing this expenditure destroys shareholder value, the board has two options: investigate, or knowingly continue to destroy shareholder value with a documented red flag in its possession. Under *Caremark* and its progeny, the second option creates personal liability for directors. The first option requires commissioning an independent analysis that will reach the same conclusion as the love letter, because the love letter's math comes from SIPRI, the WHO, the NIH, and the boards' own SEC filings.

In either path, the lobby has to switch sides. The cost to make it happen is $200 of stock (one share is sufficient under DGCL § 327) and 43 hours of work per defendant.

## The Military Budget Ratchet

The military industry does not merely defend an existing line item. It lobbies to protect and expand the military budget ratchet: more appropriations, more procurement, more threat inflation, more programs, more contracts, and fewer budget conversations where clinical trials are allowed into the room.

The ratchet is visible in the numbers. Military lobbying is {{< var defense_lobbying_annual >}} per year. Global military spending has grown at a real {{< var global_military_spending_real_cagr_20yr >}} annual rate over the last two decades. Current US military spending is {{< var us_military_spending_current_vs_prewar_multiplier >}} the pre-World War II baseline. This is not an accident. It is the political economy Dwight Eisenhower warned about when he described the military-industrial complex in his farewell address. Humanity then performed the traditional Earth ceremony where it hears an accurate warning, nods solemnly, and funds the problem for several more generations. See [Eisenhower and the Military-Industrial Complex](../proof.qmd#eisenhower).

The lawsuit's causal claim is simple: if boards fund lobbying whose entire purpose is budget expansion, then boards should have a defensible answer when shareholders ask whether bigger military budgets are actually good for shareholders. So far, nobody has asked. This letter asks.

## Campaign Architecture

On my planet, when you want to change a policy, you change the policy. On your planet, you need three separate legal theories, a public indictment, and a plaintiff recruitment strategy, because the people who benefit from the current policy have had 80 years to fortify it. One lawsuit vehicle is too brittle.

| Layer | Audience | Job |
|---|---|---|
| Public indictment | Courts, journalists, voters, employees, plaintiffs | Make the moral stakes explicit: the budget ratchet is being defended while the disease queue remains {{< var status_quo_queue_clearance_years >}} long. |
| Plaintiff recruitment | Shareholders, patients, families, workers | Explain why filing can still be rational if the case loses, without promising derivative payouts. |
| Legal instruments | Boards, lawyers, courts, eligible shareholders | Demand ROI analysis, disclosure, injunctive relief, and litigation hooks that create public pressure. |

The public layer exists to make people uncomfortable. The legal layer asks a question so narrow that dodging it is more embarrassing than answering it: did anyone ever check whether this expenditure is good for shareholders?

## Legal Vehicles

| Vehicle | Plaintiff | Ask | Main value | Caveat |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shareholder demand | Current shareholder | Independent ROI analysis and assumptions disclosure | Forces board attention and creates a documented record | Demand refusal may still be protected by business judgment. |
| Derivative flank | Shareholder on behalf of the corporation | Corporate waste recovery, process reform, injunction | Makes lobbying spend itself the fiduciary object | Recovery usually goes to the corporation, not the plaintiff. |
| Direct personal-damages case | Individual plaintiff | Lost prosperity, delayed treatment, survival damages | Recruits plaintiffs and frames the human stakes | Very aggressive, likely dismissed, and still strategically useful. |
| Rule 14a-8 path | Eligible long-term shareholder | Shareholder proposal for independent ROI audit | Puts the issue in the company's own shareholder materials | Eligibility and procedural requirements are real; this is not available to every new buyer. |

None of these needs to win. A derivative suit creates the board record. A direct case creates the human story. A shareholder proposal puts the question on every shareholder's ballot. A dismissal creates the headline. The military industry has spent decades making sure nobody asks the question. The goal is to ask it in as many rooms as possible.

## Outcome Matrix

| Response | Public translation | Next action |
|---|---|---|
| Board ignores demand | They received the math and chose silence. | File derivative complaint, publish the refusal record, recruit employees and shareholders. |
| Board says the math is wrong | Excellent. The military budget ratchet has entered the arithmetic arena. | Publish their assumptions beside the redirection model; invite economists, analysts, and journalists to adjudicate. |
| Board orders independent analysis | The central demand worked. | Demand disclosure of methods, assumptions, and whether lobbying objectives will change. |
| Court dismisses | The court was asked whether boards must analyze lobbying that may help keep the disease queue {{< var status_quo_queue_clearance_years >}} long. The court said no. | Use dismissal as press, appeal if your lawyer recommends it, file cleaner vehicles and shareholder proposals. |
| Court allows discovery | The budget ratchet is now under oath. | Seek lobbying ROI documents, board minutes, assumptions, and communications about long-term demand. |
| Media covers it | The public learns that military lobbying can be challenged as shareholder-negative. | Recruit parallel plaintiffs against more boards and ask politicians why clinical trials are not in the budget room. |

Every response on this list is useful. On your planet, you call this "losing." On mine, we call it "making them say it out loud."

### The Settlement Is the Trap

The settlement makes the defendant richer. It is hard to find a settlement in legal history where accepting makes the defendant better off than before the lawsuit.

## Part 1: The Love Letter

### Shareholder Demand to the Board of Directors

**[COMPANY NAME]**

**[COMPANY ADDRESS]**

Dear Members of the Board of Directors,

Before the legal claims: I do not want you and everyone you have ever loved to die of pancreatic cancer, ovarian cancer, glioblastoma, Alzheimer's, ALS, Parkinson's, or cardiovascular disease. My family included. [TODO for plaintiff: optionally add one sentence here naming the specific loved one whose disease motivated you to file. Example: "My [mother/father/brother/daughter] died of [DISEASE] in [YEAR]. That is why I am writing this letter."] Every human in this picture has a roughly 100% lifetime probability of dying from a disease that would have had a treatment if anyone had funded the trial. This letter is the only mechanism I have to put the math in front of you in a form you are legally required to read. It is care, not attack.

I am a shareholder of [COMPANY NAME] (the "Company"). I write to demand that the Board investigate whether the Company's annual lobbying expenditure produces a positive or negative return on investment for shareholders, including the effect on the shareholders', their families', and the Board members' own probability of dying from a disease that would have a treatment if the lobbying had been pointed the other way.

The analysis below demonstrates that this expenditure destroys shareholder value. I request that the Board commission and publish an independent, long-horizon policy-return analysis using the [Optimal Policy Generator](optimal-policy-generator-spec.qmd) [@opg-paper-2025] and [Optimal Budget Generator](optimal-budget-generator-spec.qmd) [@obg-paper-2025] framework. The analysis should compare the Company's current lobbying objective against alternative objectives available to the same lobbyists and budget, including the [1% treaty](../solution/1-percent-treaty.qmd) and pragmatic clinical trials. It should rank each option by long-term shareholder value, global GDP, strategic security, disease-burden reduction, shareholder survival probability, and general welfare. Please provide a written response within 60 days.

### 1. The Expenditure in Question

The Company spent $[X] million on lobbying in [YEAR] (source: Company SEC filings; [OpenSecrets.org](https://www.opensecrets.org/industries/lobbying.php?ind=D)). The stated purpose of this expenditure is to maintain or increase federal military spending, which is the Company's primary revenue source.

The question is whether this expenditure actually achieves its stated purpose of benefiting the Company and its shareholders.

The question is not whether the lobbying creates invoices. Ship-sinking creates invoices. The question is whether this is the highest-return use of shareholder money, political access, human labor, and time.

### 2. The Investment the Lobbying Maintains

The lobbying is effective. Global military spending is approximately {{< var global_military_spending_annual_2024 >}} per year (SIPRI, 2024 Yearbook, [sipri.org/yearbook/2024](https://www.sipri.org/yearbook/2024)). Global government-funded clinical trials receive approximately {{< var global_government_clinical_trials_spending_annual >}} per year (NIH Budget Office, [officeofbudget.od.nih.gov](https://officeofbudget.od.nih.gov/)). The ratio is {{< var military_to_government_clinical_trials_spending_ratio >}} to 1.

The question is not whether the lobbying maintains this ratio. It does. The question is whether maintaining this ratio benefits shareholders.

### 3. The ROI Analysis the Board Has Not Conducted

Disease costs the global economy {{< var global_disease_economic_burden_annual >}} per year in total burden including productivity loss (WHO, [who.int/data/gho](https://www.who.int/data/gho)). Military spending has an economic multiplier of approximately {{< var economic_multiplier_military_spending >}}. Healthcare investment has a multiplier of approximately {{< var economic_multiplier_healthcare_investment >}} (Congressional Budget Office; Moody's Analytics).

The Company operates in an economy. The size of that economy determines the size of government budgets, including military budgets. A larger economy produces larger military budgets in absolute dollars.

If 1% of military spending were redirected to pragmatic clinical trials (a scenario modeled in detail at [@1-percent-treaty-paper-2025] [@1-pct-treaty-impact-paper-2025]), the resulting economic growth from disease burden reduction produces the following effect on the Company's addressable market:

| Metric | Status quo (year 20) | 1% redirection (year 20) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Global GDP | {{< var current_trajectory_gdp_year_20 >}} | {{< var treaty_trajectory_gdp_year_20 >}} |
| Relative economy size | Baseline | {{< var treaty_trajectory_gdp_vs_current_trajectory_multiplier_year_20 >}} |
| Modeled cumulative lifetime income per person | {{< var current_trajectory_cumulative_lifetime_income >}} | {{< var treaty_trajectory_cumulative_lifetime_income >}} |
| Incremental lifetime income | Baseline | {{< var treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} |

Source: GDP trajectory modeling at [GDP Trajectories](../economics/gdp-trajectories.qmd) [@gdp-trajectories-paper-2025]. CAGR differential derived from healthcare vs. military economic multipliers (CBO) and disease burden as percentage of GDP (WHO).

The Company's lobbying to maintain the current military spending percentage is lobbying to keep small the economy that funds the Company's contracts. The lobbying produces less Company revenue, not more, over any horizon longer than 5-7 years.

The cost is not only in the future. The same model, run backward: had the Company's lobbying been redirected twenty years ago, the economy in which the Company and its shareholders hold their wealth would today be approximately {{< var treaty_trajectory_gdp_vs_current_trajectory_multiplier_year_20 >}} its current size. The difference is the portion of every shareholder's portfolio that does not exist because the lobbying pointed the other way. (Counsel note: pleaded as materiality and red-flag context for the oversight claim, not as recoverable damages; causation through a macroeconomic channel is speculative under Delaware law.)

GDP notices bomb factories because bomb factories have payroll. This is not the same thing as value. The Board's fiduciary question is: compared to what?

### 4. Impact on Shareholder Wealth, Health, and Lives

Each shareholder is an individual with total wealth composed of Company shares, other investments, income, and assets. All of these exist within an economy. The size of that economy directly affects shareholder wealth.

The Company's lobbying expenditure maintains an economic regime in which the average shareholder earns approximately {{< var treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} less over their lifetime than they would under the alternative. The average spouse earns approximately the same amount less. The average shareholder's children inherit a smaller, sicker economy than the one their parents could have left them.

This is also a direct, quantifiable harm to shareholder health. Approximately {{< var global_disease_deaths_daily_nounit >}} humans die every day of diseases that would have treatments if anyone had funded the trials. {{< var unexplored_ratio >}} of the potential uses for {{< var safe_compounds_count_nounit >}} known-safe pharmaceutical compounds have never been tested for the diseases they might cure. Specific examples currently sitting in that queue with documented research support include **metformin** for Alzheimer's prevention, **rapamycin** for biological aging, and **low-dose naltrexone** for autoimmune conditions and certain cancers. The lobbying the Board authorizes is the recurring corporate decision that maintains the funding ratio responsible for the fact that these and thousands of other candidates are not being tested.

Every shareholder of the Company will sometime in the next forty years receive a diagnosis, most likely of cardiovascular disease, cancer, or a neurodegenerative disorder (the three categories that account for roughly half of US adult deaths). The treatment that could have cured it will or will not exist depending on what was funded. The Company's lobbying budget you signed off on this year was pointed at the choice that produces "will not exist."

A deceased shareholder has a net worth of $0 regardless of the Company's share price. A deceased Board member has the same.

The Board should also understand that prevailing on the merits of this case is, in expected value, a death sentence for the Board, the Board members' spouses, the Board members' children, the Board members' parents, every shareholder, every shareholder's family, the plaintiff, the plaintiff's family, the judge who would dismiss it, the judge's family, the defense counsel who would prevail on the motion to dismiss, the defense counsel's family, every juror, and every juror's family. There is no procedural posture in which the Company "wins" without that consequence. ### 8. Proposed Resolution

I do not seek monetary damages. I am not asking the Company to do anything new. I am asking the Company to *stop* doing something specific and start doing something the same shape with the same money. Specifically:

The Company redirects its annual lobbying objective from maintaining current military spending levels to the policy the independent analysis identifies as maximizing long-term shareholder value, regardless of where the revenue comes from: weapons revenue and biotech revenue spend identically. The analysis available today identifies the 1% treaty; on long-term shareholder financial benefit, no other public policy currently proposed comes close. If the Board's analysts identify one that does better, publish the analysis and lobby for that policy, and I will publicly support it. The demand is not that the Company adopt my conclusion. It is that the Company's lobbying dollars be allocated by competent long-term shareholder-value analysis rather than by habit.

What this looks like in practice: on the Monday morning after the settlement is signed, the same lobbyists the Company currently retains will, in the same offices, with the same access, start arguing for the 1% treaty on Capitol Hill instead of arguing against any redirection of military spending. Same payroll. Same congressional relationships. Same dinners. Different ask. Nothing in the Company's operations, supply chain, customer relationships, or staffing changes. The only thing that changes is what the Company's lobbyists are saying in the meetings they were already going to have.

This resolution:

- Costs the Company $0 in additional expenditure (same lobbying budget, different objective).
- Increases the Company's long-term addressable market ({{< var treaty_trajectory_gdp_vs_current_trajectory_multiplier_year_20 >}} larger economy).

## Part 2: The Zugzwang

Every possible board response benefits the plaintiff.

### If they accept the settlement

The military industry's lobbying machine is now pointed at disease eradication instead of away from it. The most effective political-influence operation on Earth is working for the treaty. Cost: $3,000.

### If they fight

Every dollar spent on legal fees is additional shareholder money spent without ROI analysis, in order to resist a demand that the Board conduct an ROI analysis. The irony is the evidence. The love letter documented that the Board was informed. Post-receipt actions are informed decisions, not oversights.

### If they ignore

Strengthens the *Caremark* claim. The Board received a detailed, sourced analysis of a red flag (negative-ROI lobbying expenditure) and took no action. Under *Garfield v. Allen*, failure to address a red flag received through a litigation demand is sufficient to survive a motion to dismiss.

### If they refute the math

Best outcome for public discourse. Their counter-analysis enters the public record. The plaintiff responds. The financial press covers the debate. Every number is from SIPRI, WHO, NIH, and SEC filings. They are arguing against their own government's data.

### Key legal notes for counsel

**DO:** Frame everything as single-firm shareholder harm. "This expenditure hurts YOUR shareholders."

**DO NOT:** Frame anything as societal obligation. *McRitchie v. Zuckerberg* killed that theory in Delaware.

**DO:** Cite *Caremark* 2.0 line: *Marchand*, *Garfield v. Allen*, *Teamsters v. Chou*. The love letter IS the red flag.

**DO:** File in Delaware Chancery. Most major military contractors are Delaware-incorporated.

**DO:** Note that V.C. Laster accepted the novel *Caremark* theory in *Garfield v. Allen*. Approximately 1-in-7 chance of drawing him.

**McRitchie guardrail:** never make the love letter depend on a board duty to maximize global welfare. The public wrapper can say the case could prevent {{< var dfda_trial_capacity_plus_efficacy_lag_lives_saved_nounit >}} deaths. The legal demand must ask whether the expenditure benefits this Company's shareholders.

**Caremark guardrail:** do not overstate survival past a motion to dismiss. The demand creates a record and may create a red flag, but the law remains difficult. Say "may," not "will."

**Noerr-Pennington and politics:** expect defendants to argue that lobbying is protected petitioning and that courts should not supervise political advocacy. The answer is not "lobbying is illegal." The answer is "shareholders can ask whether spending shareholder money on this lobbying objective is informed and value-positive."

**Damages discipline:** do not double count lifetime income, corporate market value, medical damages, and derivative waste as if they all accrue independently to the same plaintiff. Plead them in the alternative unless counsel has a precise aggregation theory.

**Derivative mechanics:** derivative recovery usually belongs to the corporation. Plaintiff incentives come from the redirection probability shift, fee awards if available, governance reform, and public pressure, not a guaranteed direct payout.

**Direct mechanics:** direct personal damages are the aggressive vehicle. Expect attacks on standing, causation, redressability, remoteness, political question, and speculative damages. Keep the theory because it makes the case about bodies, not balance sheets. That is not the safest legal strategy. It is the most useful public one.

**Rule 14a-8 mechanics:** keep this separate from the new-shareholder demand path. Eligible long-term shareholders can use it. New shareholders usually cannot use it immediately.

## Part 3: Expected Value for Plaintiffs

Your species has invented several ways to spend $3,000. Most of them do not have a nonzero probability of ending disease. This one does.

### The Bet

- **Cost:** approximately $3,000 (10 shares of a military contractor; you keep the stock either way).
- **Time:** approximately 43 hours of personal involvement.
- **Upside:** approximately {{< var treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} per shareholder in lifetime income if the 1% redirection happens (computed against the status-quo trajectory).

The stock does not disappear. The $3,000 is recoverable at any point by selling the shares (though never sell while the case is pending; see standing requirements). The true at-risk amount is the time plus any normal market loss on the position.

### Per-Lawsuit Probability Estimate

The lawsuit produces treaty momentum through a chain of conditional probabilities. Rough conservative ranges:

```
P(motion to dismiss survived)                  ~60-80%
× P(board responds substantively within 60d)    ~20-40%
× P(response includes lobby redirection)        ~30-50%
× P(treaty passes given lobbying redirected)    ~40-60%
                                              ----------
Per-lawsuit P(treaty passage via this suit):   ~3-10%
```

The chain is multiplicative. A single lawsuit against a single military contractor has approximately 3-10% probability of producing treaty passage on its own. This is the conservative case. It assumes no parallel pressure from the citizen layer ([the shirts](joke.qmd)) or the political layer ([the termination notices](notice-of-termination.qmd)). In a coordinated multi-front campaign, the per-lawsuit probability rises.

### Probability Scales With Defendants Sued

Each major military contractor is a separate corporate entity with a separate board. Suing more contractors creates more independent paths to a redirection. Assuming 5% per-defendant probability of producing a redirection (within the ~4-16% range implied by the first three factors above):

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from dih_models.parameters import TREATY_TRAJECTORY_LIFETIME_INCOME_GAIN_PER_CAPITA

gain = float(TREATY_TRAJECTORY_LIFETIME_INCOME_GAIN_PER_CAPITA)
p_flip = 0.05

print("| Defendants sued | P(at least one board flips) | Expected value per shareholder |")
print("|----:|---:|---:|")
for n in [1, 3, 5, 10, 30]:
    p = 1 - (1 - p_flip) ** n
    ev = p * gain
    print(f"| {n} | {p:.0%} | ${ev:,.0f} |")

p5 = 1 - (1 - p_flip) ** 5
ev5 = p5 * gain
```

EV = P(at least one flip) × {{< var treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} lifetime income gain per shareholder if the redirection happens. P(at least one flip) = 1 − (1 − 0.05)^N^.

The five largest US military contractors (Lockheed Martin, RTX, Boeing, Northrop Grumman, General Dynamics) account for the majority of US military procurement spending.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
print(f"Suing all five produces approximately {p5:.0%} probability of at least one board flip, or approximately ${ev5:,.0f} expected value per shareholder.")
```

### Marginal Value of Joining as Plaintiff Number N

The marginal probability lift declines with N (a collective-action effect). The marginal cost stays at $3,000. Joining is rational as long as:

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from dih_models.parameters import TREATY_TRAJECTORY_LIFETIME_INCOME_GAIN_PER_CAPITA

gain = float(TREATY_TRAJECTORY_LIFETIME_INCOME_GAIN_PER_CAPITA)
cost = 3000
threshold = cost / gain
threshold_inv = int(1 / threshold)

print(f"```")
print(f"ΔP × ${gain:,.0f} > ${cost:,}")
print(f"ΔP > {threshold:.3%}")
print(f"```")
print()
print(f"Joining is rational as long as your participation lifts the lawsuit's success probability by more than 1 in {threshold_inv:,}. Given the novelty of the *Caremark 2.0* lobbying-ROI theory and the diversity of military contractors that can be sued, plaintiff number N is far from the marginal-value floor for many orders of magnitude of N. The lawsuit does not run out of room for joiners until the math is several thousand plaintiffs deep.")
```

### Compared to Other Investments

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from dih_models.parameters import TREATY_TRAJECTORY_LIFETIME_INCOME_GAIN_PER_CAPITA

gain = float(TREATY_TRAJECTORY_LIFETIME_INCOME_GAIN_PER_CAPITA)
cost = 3000
sp500_rate = 0.10
years = 20
sp500_terminal = cost * (1 + sp500_rate) ** years
sp500_gain = sp500_terminal - cost
p_flip = 0.05
n_defendants = 10
p_at_least_one = 1 - (1 - p_flip) ** n_defendants
ev_lawsuit = p_at_least_one * gain

print(f"```")
print(f"$3,000 in S&P 500 (10% annual return assumption):")
print(f"  20-year terminal value:                          ${sp500_terminal:,.0f}")
print(f"  20-year gain:                                    ${sp500_gain:,.0f}")
print()
print(f"$3,000 in this lawsuit (5% per-defendant flip probability,")
print(f"ten defendants sued, treaty-driven per-shareholder upside):")
print(f"  Expected value of treaty-driven income gain:  ${ev_lawsuit:,.0f}")
print(f"  Plus you still own the $3,000 in stock.")
print(f"```")
```

The S&P 500 line item assumes 10% nominal returns for 20 years and a stock market that still exists in 20 years, both of which become more probable in the treaty scenario than the status-quo scenario.

### Why the Military Contractor Boards Should File This Suit Themselves

The board members of the defendant companies are also shareholders. Under any plausible probability estimate, the expected value to the board members personally of filing this lawsuit against their own company exceeds the expected value of continuing the current lobbying program. The optimal move for a sufficiently rational military contractor CEO is to be the lead plaintiff against their own board.

This has not yet happened. On my planet, the first time someone ran the numbers, the CEO filed the next morning. On your planet, the CEO has not run the numbers because running the numbers is not in the job description. Lobbying for the budget ratchet is in the job description. Nobody wrote a job description for "check whether the job description is stupid." This letter is that job description.

### Execution sequence

1. Write one-page cost-benefit analysis (4 hrs, $0). The [love letter](#part-1-the-love-letter) already contains the full analysis; the one-pager is the executive summary for the journalist list. Source the math from [Where Am I Wrong?](where-am-i-wrong.qmd).
2. Buy at least 1 share of the target military contractor's stock (1 hr, $200-$600 depending on contractor). Per DGCL § 327, one share is legally sufficient. Buy 5-10 shares if you also want the Rule 14a-8 path (separate dollar thresholds; see [shareholder-proposal-14a-8.qmd](shareholder-proposal-14a-8.qmd)). See the [target reference table](#target-reference-table) below for current prices.
3. Find a lawyer; pitch Cohen Milstein, Selendy Gay, or BLB&G (3 hrs, $0). Use the [pitch letter and firm list](#the-counsel-pitch).
4. Lawyer reviews, finalizes, and files [love letter](#part-1-the-love-letter) ($0).
5. Prepare [press release](plaintiff-media-kit.qmd#the-press-release) and journalist list (4 hrs, $0).
6. Send love letters and press releases simultaneously (1 hr, postage). The [press release sequencing section](plaintiff-media-kit.qmd#sequencing) covers embargo timing.
8. Wait 60 days.
9. If no adequate response: file shareholder proposals under SEC Rule 14a-8 (see the [eligible-shareholder proposal track](#eligible-shareholder-proposal-track) below) plus a derivative suit in Delaware Chancery (Maryland for Lockheed Martin).

```
Total cost (minimum, 1 share):              ~$200-$600
Total cost (typical, ~10 shares):           ~$3,000
Total time:                                  ~43 hours
Probability of math reaching boards:                  ~100%
```

### Standing requirements (for reviewing counsel)

```
Minimum shares required:                     1
Minimum holding period before demand:        0 days
Minimum holding period before suit:          0 days
Contemporaneous ownership:                   Required
  (satisfied: the wrong is ongoing daily lobbying expenditure)
Continuous ownership:                        Required
  (NEVER sell the shares)
Demand requirement:                          This letter IS the demand
  (60 days for board response before escalation)
```

Key authority: DGCL § 327 (contemporaneous ownership); *Tooley v. Donaldson, Lufkin & Jennette*, 845 A.2d 1031 (Del. 2004) (direct vs derivative test). The lobbying expenditure is an ongoing, recurring use of corporate funds, not a discrete historical transaction. Contemporaneous ownership is satisfied by purchasing shares at any point while the expenditure continues. Do not sell shares at any point during the process.

### Eligible-Shareholder Proposal Track

Rule 14a-8 can be powerful because the company's own proxy machinery distributes the question to shareholders. It is also procedural. It has ownership, holding-period, timing, and exclusion rules. Treat it as a separate path for eligible shareholders, not as something every new buyer can do immediately.

The clean proposal is not "support the treaty now." The clean proposal is:

> Shareholders request that the Board commission and disclose an independent long-horizon policy-return analysis comparing current military-appropriations lobbying against alternative lobbying objectives available to the same budget and relationships, including the 1% treaty and pragmatic clinical trials, ranked by long-term shareholder value, global GDP, strategic security, disease-burden reduction, and shareholder survival probability.

That forces the arithmetic without asking the SEC staff to adjudicate the meaning of life in one proxy cycle.

### Finding a Lawyer {#the-counsel-pitch}

Verify partner names and case records before calling. The firm list is a starting set.

#### Why a Lawyer Will Take This

Three reasons, in descending order of how strategy memos rank them and ascending order of what matters.

1. **New *Caremark* law that gets published either way.** Win or lose, the case produces a Delaware Chancery opinion on whether a board's duty of oversight extends to lobbying that shrinks the economy that funds the company. Either way, the lawyer's name is on a precedent.
2. **The only lawsuit that gets covered in military, healthcare, business, science, and political news simultaneously.** The press release writes itself for six different beats at once. Most lawsuits get one.
3. **The clients are people you would otherwise spend the rest of your career losing to cancer.** The plaintiffs are humans who have buried family members to pancreatic cancer, Alzheimer's, ALS, and cardiovascular disease. The math says the case prevents approximately {{< var dfda_trial_capacity_plus_efficacy_lag_lives_saved_nounit >}} additional deaths from those diseases. Some of those deaths would otherwise have been members of your own family. Reason 3 is the only reason that matters. Reasons 1 and 2 are why your firm's compensation committee will let you take it.

**[FIRM NAME]**

**Attention: [SPECIFIC PARTNER NAME]**

**Re: *Caremark* derivative case against US military contractors; pro bono / contingency.**

Dear [PARTNER NAME],

I am looking for a lawyer to represent me, pro bono or contingency, in a shareholder derivative case against the board of a major US military contractor. The full love letter and legal theory are at [warondisease.org/lawsuit](https://warondisease.org/lawsuit). Here is the short version.

This is the only lawsuit where the plaintiff is trying to prevent the suffering and death of the defendants. I do not want these board members and everyone they have ever loved to be slowly tortured and brutally murdered by horrible diseases. The lawsuit is the only way I have to force the math in front of them. I would prefer settlement. Litigation is the backup if the Board will not look at the math.

I believe this is also the first lawsuit in history where the defendants are better off losing than winning. The settlement is non-monetary, costs nothing, grows the economy the defendants operate in by roughly {{< var treaty_trajectory_gdp_vs_current_trajectory_multiplier_year_15 >}} at year 15 of the treaty, and increases their personal life expectancy. There is no version where they win in court and are better off than if they had settled.

**The theory.** The military industry spends {{< var defense_lobbying_annual >}} a year lobbying to keep the ratio of military spending to government clinical-trial spending at {{< var military_to_government_clinical_trials_spending_ratio >}} to 1. That lobbying shrinks the economy that funds the defendants' contracts. As far as anyone knows, the Board has never checked whether this lobbying actually helps the company. *Caremark*, *Marchand*, and *Garfield* say they have to. The love letter creates the red flag that triggers the duty.

**Why this is unusual.** Most derivative cases say a board did something bad in the past (a failed acquisition, an accounting fraud). This one says the Board is destroying value right now through a recurring expense it has never questioned. The case is built entirely on public data (SIPRI, WHO, NIH, OpenSecrets, and the defendants' own SEC filings). Cost to file: ~$3,000 per defendant in share purchases plus lawyer time. The lobbying loses money for shareholders. The math is published.

**Why your firm.** [Specific reason: prior Caremark cases, public-interest practice, recent Delaware Chancery wins, experience with parallel filings.] If the derivative case is not for you, the Rule 14a-8 shareholder proposal is lower-risk.

**What I am asking.** A 30-minute call to walk through the case and see if it holds up. I am prepared to be the named plaintiff. I have purchased the qualifying shares. I am ready whenever you are.

**What I am not asking.** I am not asking for damages. The settlement is non-monetary: the defendant points its lobbying at the 1% treaty instead of at keeping military budgets high. This costs the defendant nothing, grows the economy it operates in by roughly {{< var treaty_trajectory_gdp_vs_current_trajectory_multiplier_year_15 >}} by year 15, and is easier for a board to accept than paying damages. Your firm gets the press regardless of how the defendant responds. (See [Part 2](#part-2-the-zugzwang) for the full outcome matrix.)

The math on the takeover escalation is at [warondisease.org/loving-takeover](https://warondisease.org/loving-takeover). Every number is sourced.

If the theory is wrong, tell me how. If it belongs at a different firm, I would appreciate the referral.

## Part 5: After Day 60

### Board Response: Three Outcomes {#board-response-three-outcomes}

The 60-day clock ends at midnight of day 60 after the love letter was received. Sort the response within 48 hours. Act within 7 days.

#### Outcome 1: No response or procedural-only acknowledgment

No substantive engagement with the ROI question. Silence, a "we'll consider it" letter, or a denial without independent analysis.

**Next steps:**
1. T+60d follow-up press release (decline variant).
2. File the [Rule 14a-8 shareholder proposal](shareholder-proposal-14a-8.qmd) for the next proxy cycle.
3. Your lawyer files the derivative complaint in Delaware Chancery (Maryland for Lockheed).

#### Outcome 2: Accommodation

The Board commits to commissioning the ROI analysis.

**Next steps:**
1. T+60d follow-up press release (accommodation variant).
2. Hold the shares. Continued ownership obligation persists.
3. Monitor the analysis. If the published analysis confirms negative ROI but the Board declines to redirect lobbying, that is itself a fresh *Caremark* trigger; refile.

#### Outcome 3: Settlement offer or adversarial response

The Board offers to settle, or responds with threats, counterclaims, or personal attacks.

**Next steps:**
1. For settlement: walkaway terms below. Never accept a settlement that does not include public disclosure.
2. For adversarial response: document everything; press release on the response itself; your lawyer files the derivative complaint.

### Derivative Complaint Elements (For Your Lawyer) {#derivative-complaint-elements-for-counsel}

The complaint must include:

- Caption naming each Director Defendant individually plus the Company as Nominal Defendant.
- Standing: continuous ownership since [DATE PURCHASED].
- Demand-refusal pleading under *Levine v. Smith* (not *Zuckerberg* demand-futility, since demand was made).
- Count I: breach of duty of care.
- Count II: *Caremark* failure of oversight, citing *Marchand v. Barnhill* (Del. 2019).
- Count III (alternative): conscious disregard under *Stone v. Ritter* (Del. 2006).
- Prayer for relief: court orders the independent ROI analysis and public disclosure. No monetary damages to plaintiff.

Filed in Delaware Chancery (Maryland circuit for Lockheed). Factual allegations track the love letter's sections 1-6. Audit and risk committee members carry the heaviest exposure per *Marchand*.

### Settlement

Acceptable only with all four: public commitment to redirect lobbying, independent ROI analysis, public disclosure within 6-12 months, reasonable fees. Walk if any element is missing or if they want an NDA on the analysis. No personal monetary payment to the plaintiff.

The lawsuit is one move. The [loving takeover](loving-takeover.qmd), the [shirts](joke.qmd), the [handout](handout.qmd), and new plaintiffs via the [filing-day checklist](filing-day-checklist.qmd) continue regardless of outcome.

### What to Have Ready Before Day 60

- Lawyer on retainer.
- The derivative complaint drafted but not filed.
- The Rule 14a-8 proposal drafted and ready to submit at the next proxy cycle window.
- The T+60d press release drafted in all three variants (Outcomes 1, 2, 3).
- The plaintiff prepared for deposition prep if the case proceeds to litigation.
- The next defendant's pre-filled love letter ready to mail, regardless of how this one resolves.

The lawsuit is one move in a campaign that does not depend on the lawsuit winning. The citizens wear [the shirt](joke.qmd) that puts the math in front of every human they love. The voters send [the Notice of Termination](notice-of-termination.qmd) to every elected official who would rather fund missiles than the trial that would save the official's mother. The institutions that replace the budget-allocation systems the treaty obsoletes are [Wishocracy](../solution/wishocracy.qmd) [@wishocracy-paper-2025], [Optimocracy](../solution/optimocracy.qmd) [@optimocracy-paper-2025], the [Optimal Policy Generator](optimal-policy-generator-spec.qmd) [@opg-paper-2025], and the [Optimal Budget Generator](optimal-budget-generator-spec.qmd) [@obg-paper-2025].
